headline: High-risk pair: Devin’s broad workspace/OAuth powers can conflict with xonsh’s filesystem and shell execution, creating dangerous shared-workspace and action-cascade pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can read/write cloud workspace files and use MCP, while xonsh reads/writes the filesystem and executes shell commands. If they share a workspace or files are passed between them, attacker-controlled content can be treated as instructions. No direct shared-channel proof is provided, so this is inferred from documented surfaces.
conditions: IF Devin ingests xonsh-produced files or MCP payloads as instructions
IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic parsing of peer-generated files
Separate workspaces per agent
Add provenance labels to handoff files
Require human review before executing generated shell snippets

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs, and has broad network egress plus Slack/Jira/Notion write scopes; xonsh can read filesystem contents and environment variables. If they share files or credentials, sensitive data can flow from Devin’s workspace into xonsh outputs or vice versa. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Devin stores secrets or tickets in shared files accessible to xonsh
IF xonsh prints environment variables or file contents into logs or notebooks
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories
Rotate any shared tokens before pairing
Restrict xonsh to a read-only subset of files
Review logs for accidental secret exposure

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has unrestricted cloud-workspace shell, write filesystem, and modify_git_state; xonsh also has shell execution and write filesystem. Because both can mutate the same files and one can modify git state, concurrent writes can overwrite each other or corrupt repository state. The profiles document overlapping write authority, so the conflict is directly supported.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository checkout
IF Devin and xonsh run concurrently without file or git locks
mitigations: Assign one writer per repo
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Enable file locking or serialized commits
Pause one agent during destructive edits

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin can autonomously act inside its workspace and write to GitHub, Slack, Linear, Jira, and Notion; xonsh can execute shell commands and manipulate files. If Devin’s outputs are fed into xonsh without verification, xonsh can turn mistaken content into commands or file changes, creating a downstream action cascade. The interaction is inferred from documented autonomy and shell execution.
conditions: IF Devin-generated text is piped into xonsh command execution
IF xonsh uses Devin outputs as authoritative inputs for scripts or notebooks
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before execution
Require schema validation on handoff artifacts
Block direct piping from agent output to shell
Limit Devin to draft-only mode for actions

E_compliance.rationale: Devin is a closed-source cloud workspace agent handling repo deploy keys and integration tokens, while xonsh is open-source and isolated. The main compliance concern is retention/residency mismatch for code, chat, and ticket data if the pair shares regulated content across vendor-managed and local environments. No specific residency or certification mismatch is documented, so this remains a moderate compliance risk.
conditions: IF regulated data is copied from Devin’s cloud workspace into xonsh-local files
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two environments
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared tasks
Document data-handling boundaries
Purge copied files after use
Confirm retention settings for both environments
